messages.author: 067e97ce536c222f
messages.subject: Error in inla.create.sn.cache() : inla.require("sn") is not TRUE
parts:
Hello,
I am trying to run one of the practicals for inlabru using the following:
data(gorillas, package = "inlabru")
nests <- gorillas$nests
mesh <- gorillas$mesh
boundary <- gorillas$boundary
matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh, 
                              prior.sigma = c(0.1, 0.01), 
                              prior.range = c(5, 0.01))
cmp <- coordinates ~ mySmooth(map = coordinates,
                              model = matern) +
                          Intercept

fit <- lgcp(cmp, nests, samplers = boundary)

lambda <- predict(fit, pixels(mesh), ~ exp(mySmooth + Intercept))

The predict function fails with the following error:
Error in inla.create.sn.cache() : inla.require("sn") is not TRUE

I can't seem to find a help file for that error or any reference to either function and so don't know what might be going wrong. Any insight as to what's going on here would be most appreciated. Session info below if it's helpful.

parts: It appears that a number of the dependencies (e.g., 'graph' and 'RgraphViz') have been removed from cran (including old versions)? There are also some references to a problem with gfortran when installing mnormt. I've had to do some fiddling with my compilers to make Stan run on Catalina, so this may be part of the issue. I'm going to see if updating fixes things, but leave this here in case someone else runs into this. Will report back after the update.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.create.sn.cache() : inla.require("sn") is not TRUE
parts: I was able to get this older version of mnormt to install on 3.6: https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/contrib/3.6/mnormt_1.5-7.zip. Then I reinstalled sn and all is well.

On Wednesday, July 8, 2020 at 2:00:22 PM UTC-6, Matt Williamson wrote:
Just to close the loop on this, updating to R4.0 allowed for a clean install of all of the packages and dependencies. This appears to have eliminated the error. I wasn't able to successfully install the legacy versions of the required packages on R3.6, but that may be my own failing... Thanks for your help.

Graph and Graphviz is part of the bioconductor project. You can ignore those for the time being.
